summary:
Guam stands under the full United States federal framework as an unincorporated US territory. United States passports and other federal travel documents reflect sex assigned at birth, and the X gender marker was eliminated by a January 2025 executive order, so a trans visitor travelling on United States documents faces a mismatch between document and presentation at entry.

Screening at Guam's airport follows Transport Security Administration procedure, which applies in Guam as a US territory. The agency's body-scanner and pat-down protocols can disclose a trans traveller's status to officers. Travellers may request an alternative screening method and escalate problems on the spot, and most trans travellers pass screening without incident.

The January 2025 executive order halting federal funding for gender-affirming care reaches federally funded institutions in Guam, so access to that care during a visit can be constrained by federal policy rather than local practice.

A separate January 2025 executive order bans transgender troops from serving openly and directs the Secretary of Defense to submit an implementation plan within 30 days; the order frames trans identity as "radical gender ideology." It applies in Guam, which hosts a large permanent United States military presence, and signals the federal posture a visitor can expect from official institutions on the island.

On partner recognition, Guam's prohibition on same-sex marriage was struck down in June 2015, and the territory became the first US territory to recognise same-sex marriage.
tangentialFactors:
The June 2015 ruling came from chief judge Frances M Tydingco-Gatewood, who invalidated Guam's same-sex marriage prohibition after an April 2015 lawsuit by Loretta Pangelinan and Kathleen Aguero, who had been denied a marriage licence; the ruling took effect at 8am on Tuesday 9 June 2015.

Guam's status as the first US territory to recognise same-sex marriage places its relationship law ahead of several other US territories, while its criminal, document and screening regimes remain those of the United States rather than local enactments.

The military executive order's language casting trans identity as "radical gender ideology" is a statement of federal framing, and Guam's large permanent military presence means that framing is unusually visible in the territory's institutions and workforce.
localsOnly:
Guam residents hold United States citizenship and travel on United States passports, so the elimination of the X marker and the retention of sex assigned at birth on federal documents affect residents' own identity paperwork, not only visitors'.

Residents serving in the United States military fall under the January 2025 open-service ban and its 30-day implementation plan, and local residents employed by federally funded healthcare institutions are subject to the federal funding conditions on gender-affirming care.

Guam's own marriage law has recognised same-sex marriage since the June 2015 district court ruling, so resident couples marry under a locally effective regime rather than a federal default.
outOfScopeNotes:
The source inventory does not resolve whether Guam's local statutes provide hate-crime enhancement for offences motivated by gender identity, or whether any local non-discrimination ordinance covers gender identity in employment, housing or public accommodations. Those questions are not sourced here.

No source in the inventory addresses Guam-specific rules for changing a gender marker on a local birth certificate or driver's licence, nor whether a local facility policy governs restroom access; the federal document position is sourced, the local one is not.

Two listed sources, a Pacific sexual-identity research guide and a document-guide page for Guam, yielded no usable finding for this record, so they neither support nor contradict the claims above.

Enforcement practice at the airport is described only in general terms by a national know-your-rights guide; no Guam-specific complaint data or incident record is available in the inventory.
